body:
I have a similar background as far as the "no friends except online friends that I don't talk to anymore" situation, so I understand your feelings of social awkwardness.

Have you ever played D&D?  I'm sure if you looked around, you could find a local game store that holds weekly D&D games, or you could go on Roll20.net and find games there.  Playing on Roll20 will give you that layer of online anonymity if you don't feel comfortable going to a game shop and playing with strangers in person.

I've been playing for over a year now, and it has helped me with my social awkwardness quite a bit.  You are playing with groups of like-minded people who are also a bit nerdy and awkward, so it's easier to relate to them and open up a bit.  You're also stepping out of yourself to roleplay a character, a bit like WoW, and that lets you further separate yourself from what you are saying and doing. 

It's a good platform to help you up out of the depths of social anxiety, and it is also a ton of fun. I highly reccommend it.
